metaDescription: Free online Percentage Difference Calculator. Calculate the absolute percentage difference between two numbers when neither is clearly the 'original' value.
intro: Comparing two numbers and want to know how far apart they are? Our free Percentage Difference Calculator gives you the precise absolute percentage difference between any two values.
whatIs: The Percentage Difference Calculator is a statistical tool used to compare two values when neither value is distinctly considered the 'starting point' or 'original'. It measures how completely different they are relative to their average.
howToUse: Enter the first value into Value A.
Enter the second value into Value B.
The order does not matter. The tool instantly computes the absolute percentage difference.
howItWorks: The tool takes the absolute difference between the two numbers (|A - B|). It then calculates the average of the two numbers ((A + B) / 2). Finally, it divides the absolute difference by the average and multiplies by 100.
workedExample: Comparing 40 and 60. Absolute difference is 20. The average is 50. (20 / 50) = 0.40. Multiply by 100. The percentage difference between 40 and 60 is 40%.
resultInterpretation: The result is a neutral percentage that tells you how different the two numbers are from each other, regardless of which direction the change happened.
useCases: Science & Engineering: Comparing an experimental test result against a theoretical prediction.
Quality Control: Measuring the difference between the size of a manufactured part and the design blueprint.
Opinion Polling: Measuring the spread between two competing election candidates.
tipsAndLimitations: Percentage Difference is completely different from Percentage Change. Use this tool only when you are comparing two independent things, not one thing changing over time.
The result will always be a positive number.

faq.question: What is the formula for percentage difference?
faq.answer: Formula: (|Value A - Value B| / ((Value A + Value B) / 2)) × 100.

faq.question: Why does order not matter?
faq.answer: Because the formula uses the absolute difference (always a positive number) and divides by the average, entering 40 then 60 yields the exact same result as entering 60 then 40.

disclaimer: This tool strictly applies the absolute difference divided by the average formula. Ensure you do not actually need Percentage Change.
